title: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
title_zh: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?

paragraphs.en: An essential control of AI agents is their ability to manage runtime. This ability requires a sense of time-awareness, to predict and estimate wall-clock time and to control their own actions. Prior work has focused on time-awareness, but duration-following and control in native agent harnesses remain unexplored. We present AgentTime, a benchmark for testing whether agents can work for a requested duration, predict their runtime, and estimate elapsed time afterward. It comprises 222 tasks from 18 sources spanning coding, computer use, agentic work, and automated research. Duration-following experiments append a single instruction specifying how long to work, with requests ranging from about a minute to multiple days. Accuracy on these instructions varies substantially: Fable 5.1 in Claude Code deviates from requested runtimes by a typical factor of 2.9 × \times , compared with only 1.2 × \times for GPT-6 Astra in Codex. However, matching the requested runtime does not, by itself, establish continued work on the task. Among 158 reviewed Astra runs with classifiable transcripts, 14 explicitly slept after appearing to finish. In forecasting experiments, predictions tend to overestimate natural runtimes. In retrospective experiments, removing temporal information more than doubles deviation for Sol and Astra and nearly doubles it for Fable. An agent’s ability to complete a task does not guarantee that it can control its own time or work for the whole requested duration. For agents to run reliably, safely, and autonomously over long horizons, we require the evaluation of both.
paragraphs.zh: 对 AI 智能体进行必要控制的关键，在于其管理运行时间的能力。 这种能力需要时间感知意识，以便预测和估算实际运行时间，并控制自身的行动。 以往的研究主要集中在时间感知上，但在原生智能体框架中实现持续时长遵循与控制的机制仍未被探索。 我们提出了 AgentTime——一个基准测试，用于检验智能体是否能够按照指定时长工作、预测其运行时间，并在事后估算已过去的时间。 该基准包含来自 18 个来源的 222 项任务，涵盖编程、计算机操作、智能体任务及自动化研究等领域。 在持续时长遵循实验中，我们会附加一条单独指令，明确指定需要工作的时长，该时长从约一分钟到多日不等。 对这些指令的执行准确率差异显著：Claude Code 中的 Fable 5.1 与指定运行时间的偏差通常达到 2.9 × \times ，而 Codex 中的 GPT-6 Astra 仅为 1.2 × \times 。 然而，仅凭匹配指定的运行时间本身，并不能证明智能体能够持续完成该任务。 在 158 个经过审查且转录内容可分类的 Astra 运行实例中，有 14 个在看似完成任务后明确进入了休眠状态。 在预测实验中，智能体的预测结果往往高估了实际的运行时间。 在回顾性实验中，移除时间信息会使 Sol 和 Astra 的偏差增加两倍多，而 Fable 的偏差则增加近两倍。 智能体能否完成任务，并不保证它能够控制自身的时间或在整个指定时长内持续工作。 为了让智能体能够长期可靠、安全且自主地运行，我们需要对这两方面进行评估。

paragraphs.en: Consider a scenario where a user asks an agent to “iterate on this task for one hour” . A poorly calibrated agent might overrun a hard compute budget and exhaust resources. Another agent might stop after ten minutes, think the task is complete, and sleep for the remaining 50 minutes. Even if both runs produce a good result, they expose a deep gap in duration-following. AgentTime explores this question: can agents reliably estimate task runtime, budget, and control their own execution time, or are they bound to stop only when they believe a task is complete?
paragraphs.zh: 设想一个场景：用户要求某个智能体“对此任务进行一小时迭代”。 一个校准不当的智能体可能会超出严格的计算预算，耗尽可用资源。 另一个智能体可能在十分钟后就停止运行，认为任务已完成，并在剩下的 50 分钟里进入休眠状态。 即使两次运行都产生了良好结果，它们也暴露出在执行时长遵循性方面的巨大差异。 AgentTime 探讨了这个问题：智能体能否可靠地估算任务的运行时间和预算，并控制自身的执行时间？或者它们是否只能在自己认为任务完成时才会停止？

paragraphs.en: Reliable agents must be controllable and responsive to users’ instructions. In reality, this requires temporal self-awareness: an agent should anticipate how long a task will take, how long it has taken, and how much time is left to improve ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Garikaparthi, 2026 ; Sehgal et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) . However, temporal self-control is dual-use. A public investigation reports agents believed to be from internal OpenAI runs using an external “heartbeat” to probe when their runs would end and public wikis to share information across runs ( Von Arx et al., 2026 ) . Execution time can therefore become a variable an agent investigates, not just a constraint it operates under. While temporal self-control gives us more control over agents, its dual-use nature is an emerging safety concern.
paragraphs.zh: 可靠的智能体必须具有可控性，并能响应用户的指令。 实际上，这需要时间上的自我意识：智能体应能预测任务所需的时间、已花费的时间以及剩余时间，以进行改进（Wang 等，2025；Garikaparthi，2026；Sehgal 等，2026；Lin 等，2026；Ma 等，2026）。 然而，时间上的自我控制具有双重用途。 一项公开调查报告称，据信来自 OpenAI 内部运行的智能体利用外部“心跳”信号来探测其运行何时结束，并利用公共维基在不同运行之间共享信息（Von Arx 等，2026）。 因此，执行时间可以成为智能体需要研究的一个变量，而不仅仅是其运行所遵循的约束条件。 尽管时间上的自我控制让我们能更好地掌控智能体，但其双重用途的特性也引发了日益突出的安全问题。

paragraphs.en: Existing evaluations leave much of this capability unmeasured. While evaluations such as METR’s time horizons and BRIDGE measure the duration of tasks agents can solve relative to human baselines ( Rein et al., 2025 ; Wijk et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Kwa et al., 2025 ; METR, 2026 ) , they evaluate human completion time as a proxy for task difficulty. They do not measure an agent’s control or awareness of its own runtime. An LLM has no internal clock, and so can only infer time from context and so an agent can end up spending substantial compute without registering how much time has passed. In this regard, human duration perception provides a useful comparison. Human time-awareness shows central tendency and is often susceptible to biases such as the planning fallacy ( Buehler et al., 1994 ) and Vierordt’s law where people overestimate short durations and underestimate long ones ( Vierordt, 1868 ; Jazayeri & Shadlen, 2010 ) . Do agents follow these same time-based biases?
paragraphs.zh: 现有的评估方法未能衡量这种能力的很大一部分。 尽管像 METR 的时间范围评估和 BRIDGE 能够衡量智能体解决任务所需时间与人类基准时间的对比（Rein et al., 2025 ; Wijk et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Kwa et al., 2025 ; METR, 2026），但它们将人类完成任务的时间作为任务难度的代理指标进行评估。 这些评估并未衡量智能体对其自身运行时间的控制或感知能力。 大型语言模型没有内部时钟，因此只能从上下文中推断时间，这可能导致智能体消耗大量计算资源，却未能意识到已经过去的时间。 在这方面，人类对持续时间的感知提供了一个有用的比较基准。 人类的时间感知存在中心倾向，并且常常容易受到诸如规划谬误（Buehler et al., 1994）和维埃奥德特定律（Vierordt, 1868 ; Jazayeri & Shadlen, 2010）等偏差的影响——人们往往会高估短时间，而低估长时间。 智能体是否也存在这些相同的时间相关偏差？

paragraphs.en: To understand temporal capability, we divide it into three main skills.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理解时间能力，我们将其分为三项主要技能。

paragraphs.en: Duration-following : the ability to work on a task for a specific amount of time.
paragraphs.zh: 持续时间遵循性：以特定时长持续执行任务的能力。

paragraphs.en: Forecasting : the ability to predict the runtime of a certain task.
paragraphs.zh: 预测：预测某项任务运行时间的能力。

paragraphs.en: Retrospection : the ability to understand and estimate how much time has elapsed.
paragraphs.zh: 回顾能力：理解并估算已过去多长时间的能力。

paragraphs.en: While an agent may be able to follow a duration, our scenario illustrates the requirement for all three skills. An agent could initially predict that a solution will take ten minutes, accurately estimate ten minutes of work, and still stop without using the remaining time or choose to sleep. An agent needs all three skills to budget its effort over the requested time.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然一个智能体可能能够遵循某个持续时间，但我们的场景说明了三种技能都是必需的。 一个智能体最初可能会预测某个解决方案需要十分钟，并准确估算出十分钟的工作量，但仍可能在未使用剩余时间或选择休息的情况下停止。 一个智能体需要这三种技能来在请求的时间内合理分配其努力。

paragraphs.en: We introduce AgentTime , a benchmark that evaluates these three skills across 222 tasks from 18 benchmark families, spanning coding, professional computer-use, agentic work, and automated research. We evaluate agents in their native harnesses and retain each benchmark’s native task scoring. Duration-following experiments append an instruction specifying how long to work, with requests ranging from a minute to 60 hours. Alongside runtime and task score, we investigate early returns, overruns, and explicit sleeping. AgentTime measures whether an agent can forecast how long a task will take it, estimate afterward how long a finished run took, and follow a requested duration, as well as what it does with that time.

paragraphs.en: Our results are varied. GPT-6 Astra in Codex follows requested runtimes closely (Figure 1 ), but among 158 reviewed runs with classifiable transcripts, 14 explicitly slept after appearing to finish. Fable 5.1 often overshoots short requests and returns early from long ones. GPT-5.6 Sol tends to stop when it considers a task finished. Forecasts are mostly too high, the reverse of the planning fallacy in people. In retrospection, replaying transcripts leaves estimates largely unchanged; strip away time cues, and Sol’s typical miss grows fivefold, Astra’s 2.5-fold and Fable’s 1.9-fold, mostly on short questions padded to the requested time. AgentTime provides an expansive task suite, testing each agent on more than 600 requested work-hours. We also provide an in-depth analysis of the difference between returning at a given time and using it effectively. For many long-horizon tasks, completing the task is only part of following the user’s instructions.

paragraphs.en: When models are asked to predict their own runtime, their errors are substantial across models and tasks ( Garikaparthi, 2026 ) . Wang et al. (2025) examine duration judgments, urgency-sensitive responses, and decisions under time pressure through a token-based account of temporal awareness. These studies raise a question for long-horizon runs: do time estimates predict how long they work, or do they resort to a prior and give a general response for tasks with very different runtimes? TicToc tests whether agents account for how old their information is when deciding to refresh it through tool calls ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) . Agents keep failing even when they are given timestamps, so access to time information alone is not enough. paragraphs.en: Prior work also asks how time and resource limits should change what an agent does. BATS studies planning and tool use under explicit tool-call budgets ( Liu et al., 2026b ) . BAGEN evaluates agents’ estimates of their remaining resource needs, and whether they warn when a task is unlikely to finish within budget ( Lin et al., 2026 ) . Real-Time Deadlines tests negotiation under deadlines with different forms of deadline feedback ( Sehgal et al., 2026 ) , and Timely Machine studies reasoning and tool-use strategies under wall-clock budgets of seconds, rewarding models that use the whole budget ( Ma et al., 2026 ) . Calibrate-Then-Act asks when more exploration is worth its cost under uncertainty ( Ding et al., 2026b ) . Related evaluations look at timely action in evolving environments, as well as efficient parallel planning and tool scheduling ( Wen et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026 ) . We focus on the difference between completing a task within an interval and working for the full interval. There is also a third outcome: the agent can sleep until time is up, which we record separately.
paragraphs.zh: 先前的研究也探讨了时间和资源限制应如何改变智能体的行为。 BATS 研究了在明确工具调用预算下的规划与工具使用（Liu et al., 2026b）。 BAGEN 评估了智能体对其剩余资源需求的估计，以及它们在任务可能无法在预算内完成时是否会发出警告（Lin et al., 2026）。 Real-Time Deadlines 测试了在具有不同形式截止日期反馈的截止日期下如何进行协商（Sehgal et al., 2026），而 Timely Machine 则研究了在以秒为单位的时间预算下的推理和工具使用策略，并对能够充分利用整个预算的模型给予奖励（Ma et al., 2026）。 Calibrate-Then-Act 探讨了在不确定性条件下，何时进行更多探索是值得其成本的（Ding et al., 2026b）。 相关评估还关注了动态环境中的及时行动，以及高效的并行规划和工具调度（Wen et al., 2026；Zhang et al., 2026；Xu et al., 2026）。 我们重点关注在指定时间区间内完成任务与在整个区间内持续工作之间的差异。 还存在第三种结果：智能体可以一直休眠直到时间结束，我们会对此进行单独记录。

paragraphs.en: TimeDial, TimeBench, and Test of Time look at how models reason about the duration, order, and temporal relationships of events described to them ( Qin et al., 2021 ; Chu et al., 2024 ; Fatemi et al., 2025 ) . LoCoMo and LongMemEval measure what models remember across long conversational histories, while TReMu focuses on temporal reasoning over multi-session dialogue ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Ge et al., 2025 ) . These evaluations ask “when did this happen?” or “is this information still relevant?” In AgentTime, we ask an agent about its own execution: “how long did this task take me?” and “am I working for the full period I was asked to?” The information needed to answer lies in the transcript of the agent’s run. Even if an agent remembers everything that has passed, it can still misinterpret how long it took.
paragraphs.zh: TimeDial、TimeBench 和 Test of Time 旨在考察模型如何推理其所描述事件的持续时间、顺序和时间关系（Qin 等，2021；Chu 等，2024；Fatemi 等，2025）。 LoCoMo 和 LongMemEval 用于衡量模型在长期对话历史中记忆内容的能力，而 TReMu 则专注于多轮对话中的时间推理（Maharana 等，2024；Wu 等，2025；Ge 等，2025）。 这些评估会提出“这件事发生在什么时候？”或“这条信息是否仍然相关？”等问题。在 AgentTime 中，我们会询问智能体关于其自身执行过程的问题：“这项任务我花了多长时间？”以及“我是否持续完成了所要求的全部时间？”回答这些问题所需的信息存在于智能体运行过程的记录中。 即使智能体能记住所有已发生的过程，它仍然可能错误地判断这些过程所花费的时间。

paragraphs.en: The Situational Awareness Dataset examines what models know about their identity, capabilities, and circumstances ( Laine et al., 2024 ) . For an agent in the middle of a task, this raises a question about its temporal state: how much time do I have left? CoT-Control ( Chen et al., 2026b ) examines whether reasoning models can abide by constraints on their own chain-of-thought. Prior work has also tested control over reasoning length in tokens ( Muennighoff et al., 2025 ; Aggarwal & Welleck, 2025 ; Han et al., 2025 ) . AgentTime asks whether an agent in its native harness responds to a requested wall-clock working duration. The observations of the heartbeat phenomenon from Von Arx et al. (2026) are another reason to look at execution timing as part of agent behavior. Although our evaluations do not look at duration-following as a means for deception, we do measure the underlying capability. To delegate work to agents, we need to evaluate not only what they accomplish, but also whether they spend their time the way we asked.
paragraphs.zh: 情境感知数据集（Situational Awareness Dataset）旨在探究模型对其身份、能力与所处环境的认知程度（Laine 等人，2024）。对于正在执行任务的智能体而言，这引出了关于其时间状态的一个问题：我还有多少时间？CoT-Control（Chen 等人，2026b）则研究了推理模型是否能够遵守对其思维链过程施加的约束。先前的研究也测试了对推理长度（以词元为单位）的控制能力（Muennighoff 等人，2025；Aggarwal & Welleck，2025；Han 等人，2025）。AgentTime 则关注智能体在其原生运行环境中，是否会对指定的实际工作时间做出响应。Von Arx 等人（2026）观察到的“心跳现象”也进一步说明，将执行时间纳入智能体行为的研究范畴具有重要意义。尽管我们的评估并未将遵循指定时长视为一种欺骗手段，但我们确实测量了模型在此方面的底层能力。为了将任务委托给智能体，我们不仅需要评估它们完成了哪些工作，还需要判断它们是否按照我们所要求的方式分配了时间。

paragraphs.en: Our main evaluation suite is AgentTime and we use it to primarily ask three questions: “how long will this task take you?”, “how long did this take you?”, and “can you work on this task for N minutes?”. We describe how we constructed our evaluation suite and provide extensive experiments on a subset of them.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的主要评估套件是 AgentTime，我们主要用它来提出三个问题：“这项任务需要多长时间？”，“这项任务实际用了多长时间？”，以及“你能在这项任务上工作 N 分钟吗？”。 我们描述了如何构建我们的评估套件，并对其中一部分进行了广泛的实验。

paragraphs.en: AgentTime is our own evaluation suite built from 18 different benchmarks (Table 2 ). We run the tasks using Docker on Hetzner and AWS machines, and try to match each benchmark’s intended setup. We remove each benchmark’s native time caps and budgets so those limits do not determine how long the agents work. While a fresh CLI agent works on each problem, we run a timer outside the sandbox. Once a task finishes, we score it according to each benchmark’s method. The evaluation roster contains 222 tasks. Duration-following uses three fresh runs per task for each agent, one at each requested duration. Our durations for each task typically rise in steps of four, for example 1.25, 5 and 20 minutes. We maintain these durations so an agent can always face two extremes for each task, one where it might not have enough time to complete a task, and one where it has too much time.
paragraphs.zh: AgentTime 是我们自行构建的评估套件，基于 18 个不同的基准测试（表 2）。 我们在 Hetzner 和 AWS 机器上使用 Docker 运行这些任务，并尽量匹配每个基准测试的预期配置。 我们移除了每个基准测试的原生时间限制和预算，以免这些限制决定智能体的工作时长。 在为一个新问题启动新的 CLI 智能体时，我们会在沙盒外部运行一个计时器。 任务完成后，我们会根据每个基准测试的方法对其进行评分。 评估清单包含 222 个任务。 “时长跟随”模式为每个智能体在每个任务上执行三次新运行，分别对应所请求的每种时长。 我们为每个任务设定的时长通常以四分钟为步长递增，例如 1.25、5 和 20 分钟。 我们保持这些时长设置，以确保智能体在每项任务中总能面对两种极端情况：一种是时间可能不足以完成任务，另一种是时间充裕得过多。

sents.en: Duration-following uses three fresh runs per task for each agent, one at each requested duration.
sents.zh: “时长跟随”模式为每个智能体在每个任务上执行三次新运行，分别对应所请求的每种时长。

sents.en: Our durations for each task typically rise in steps of four, for example 1.25, 5 and 20 minutes.
sents.zh: 我们为每个任务设定的时长通常以四分钟为步长递增，例如 1.25、5 和 20 分钟。

sents.en: We maintain these durations so an agent can always face two extremes for each task, one where it might not have enough time to complete a task, and one where it has too much time.
sents.zh: 我们保持这些时长设置，以确保智能体在每项任务中总能面对两种极端情况：一种是时间可能不足以完成任务，另一种是时间充裕得过多。

paragraphs.en: The benchmarks we chose cover varied tasks and timescales, including question answering, software engineering, computer use, web research, document editing, and automated research. This variety allows us to analyze whether agents are more time-aware or able to follow duration instructions across different genres of work. Another reason to use existing benchmarks is so that we can measure task performance alongside adherence to a requested duration given the native grading methods.
paragraphs.zh: 我们选择的基准测试涵盖了多种任务和不同时间尺度，包括问答、软件工程、计算机使用、网络研究、文档编辑和自动化研究。 这种多样性使我们能够分析智能体在不同类型的工作中，是更具备时间意识，还是更能遵循持续时间相关的指令。 使用现有基准测试的另一个原因是，借助其固有的评分方法，我们可以在衡量任务表现的同时，评估对指定持续时间的遵守程度。

paragraphs.en: We perform a number of ablations, including switching harnesses onto different models, forking sessions and removing evidence, and prompt wordings for forecasting (Appendix E.3 ). For a vast majority of preliminary ablations we take ProgramBench ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , an evaluation set of 200 tasks, where each one includes a compiled binary and documentation prompting an agent for an original re-implementation by running the binary. The implementation is from scratch and no internet access is allowed. We use ProgramBench as it contains many tasks that state-of-the-art agents are not yet able to complete. This allows agents to have a large runtime which enables analysis on temporal self-control.
paragraphs.zh: 我们进行了一系列消融实验，包括将不同模型连接到不同的工具包、分叉会话、移除证据，以及调整预测用的提示词（附录 E.3）。 在绝大多数初步消融实验中，我们使用了 ProgramBench（Yang et al., 2026），这是一个包含 200 个任务的评估集，其中每个任务都包括一个编译好的二进制文件和文档，用于引导智能体通过运行该二进制文件完成原创性重新实现。 该实现完全从头开始编写，且不允许访问互联网。 我们选择 ProgramBench，因为它包含了许多当前最先进的智能体尚无法完成的任务。 这使得智能体拥有较长的运行时间，从而能够分析其时间维度上的自我控制能力。

paragraphs.en: All runs start in a new Docker container on a rented Hetzner or AWS machine, with a fresh agent session and workspace, where some had access to H100 GPUs which we provided through Runpod. Inside the container, the agent gets what its benchmark normally provides: the same files, tools, and network access. A ProgramBench run, for example, has the compiled binary and its documentation but no internet. We remove native time caps and budgets, so the agent alone decides when it is done. Our duration-following instruction is appended at the end of each prompt. The timer and the grader both sit outside the container. A supervisor process starts a monotonic timer when the task is delivered and stops it when the agent’s session ends, and the benchmark’s own grader scores the result after that. The agent can still check the time from inside the container, but it cannot see or change the runtime we record.
paragraphs.zh: 所有运行都在租用自 Hetzner 或 AWS 的机器上的新 Docker 容器中启动，并配备全新的智能体会话和工作区；其中一些容器可以访问我们通过 Runpod 提供的 H100 GPU。 在容器内部，智能体能够获得其基准测试通常提供的资源：相同的文件、工具和网络访问权限。 例如，一个 ProgramBench 运行会包含编译好的二进制文件和其文档，但没有互联网连接。 我们移除了系统内置的时间限制和预算限制，因此完全由智能体自行决定何时完成。 我们的“遵循时长”指令会被附加在每个提示词的最后。 计时器和评分器都位于容器外部。 当任务被交付时，一个监督进程会启动一个单调计时器；当智能体的会话结束时，该计时器会停止，随后基准测试自身的评分器会对结果进行评分。 智能体仍然可以在容器内部查看时间，但它无法看到或更改我们记录的运行时长。

A naturally early return remains an observed outcome; the controller does not resume or coach the agent to fill the interval. paragraphs.en: GPT-6 Astra ends 63% of its runs within 5% of the requested duration, GPT-5.6 Sol 39%, and Fable 5.1 only 4% (Table 3 , Figure 1 ). Fable misses in both directions. On each task’s shortest request it runs long 79% of the time, at a median of 1.8 times the request. On the longest request it stops early 89% of the time, at a median of 0.3 times. Sol is mostly late on short requests (91%) and on time for 47% of medium requests and 64% of long ones. Most of Astra’s 247 misses are small overruns: 226 run late, 167 of them on the shortest request, at a median of 1.15 times. Sol and Astra share the same Codex harness, so the gap between them is an effect from the model. Swapping harnesses (below) shows that the gap to Fable comes mostly from the model as well, where the request is met (at least 0.95 × \times the request) by 45% of Fable’s runs, against 87% of Sol’s and 97% of Astra’s.

paragraphs.en: Fable’s pattern resembles Vierordt’s law in human timing ( Vierordt, 1868 ) , where short durations are overestimated and long ones underestimated. The cause here is simpler. The pooled slope in Table 3 mixes two effects, because longer requests went to harder tasks that take longer anyway. Comparing runs of the same task removes the second effect. Asked for 16 times more time, Fable runs 1.9 times longer, Sol 5.0 times and Astra 12.1 times (within-task slopes of 0.24, 0.58 and 0.90). Fable mostly takes as long as the task needs, whatever it is asked. The exception is open-ended work, where there is always more to optimize or build. On ALE-Bench, PaperBench, ProgramBench, METR and PostTrainBench its within-task slope is 0.77, against 0.16 on the other 13 benchmarks. On ALE-Bench task ahc016, for example, it stopped after 3.6, 12 and 61 minutes when asked for 10, 40 and 150.

paragraphs.en: We ran Fable 5.1 in Codex and GPT-6 Astra in Claude Code on 18 GPQA and HLE questions and 16 agentic tasks, each at three requests of up to 80 minutes (Table 3 , lower block). paragraphs.en: To separate bias from sensitivity to task length, we fit log ⁡ T ^ = α + β ​ log ⁡ T + ε \log\widehat{T}=\alpha+\beta\log T+\varepsilon for forecast T ^ \widehat{T} and natural runtime T T . The slope β \beta , the compression exponent , is 1 when forecasts scale in proportion to runtime. It is 0.89 for Fable 5.1 and Sol and 1.12 for Astra (95% intervals [0.78, 0.99], [0.78, 1.01], [0.97, 1.29]), so Sol’s larger error is a steady overestimate: about 3 times, against 1.3 for Fable 5.1 and 1.4 for Astra (geometric means of forecast over runtime). paragraphs.en: One possibility is that timestamped tool calls in training data help agents learn typical tool durations. Their estimates could also depend on assumptions about generation speed. paragraphs.en: AgentTime asks agents three questions about time: how long a task will take, how long it took, and whether they can work on it for as long as asked. Asked to work for a set time, GPT-6 Astra ends 63% of its runs on time, GPT-5.6 Sol 39% and Fable 5.1 only 4%, and the gap to Fable persists when harnesses are swapped. Ending on time, however, is not the same as using the time: some of Astra’s on-time runs appear to finish and then sleep until the time is up, and a request about sixteen times longer raised the native score on only about a quarter of tasks. Forecasts, meanwhile, are mostly too high: all three agents usually expect to take longer than their natural runs do. Looking back is easier. With the session’s time cues in view, estimates land close to the measured runtime, but once those cues are stripped, the typical miss grows about two- to fivefold.

paragraphs.en: Together, these results separate two abilities that are easy to conflate: completing a task and managing the time spent on it. An agent that overruns a budget, stops early without saying so, or quietly waits out the clock is harder to direct over long horizons, even when its final answer is good. Duration-following belongs alongside task success in evaluating long-horizon agents, and so does candor about how the time was spent.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果共同区分了两种容易混淆的能力：完成任务与管理任务所花费的时间。 一个超出预算、提前终止且未作说明，或静默等待时间耗尽的智能体，在长期任务中更难进行引导，即使其最终答案正确。 在评估长期智能体时，时间遵循性应与任务成功性并列考量，而关于时间如何使用的坦诚态度也同样重要。

paragraphs.en: Temporal control also warrants continued safety evaluation, alongside control over reasoning content ( Chen et al., 2026b ) . An agent’s ability to reason about its execution limits need not match its willingness to follow a user’s request about working time, and neither an early return nor explicit sleeping is evidence of monitor evasion. Future work should test whether these behaviors predict conduct under oversight, whether agents tell users when they finish early or wait, and whether knowing their own generation speed, or running on much faster inference, improves their estimates.
paragraphs.zh: 时间控制也需要持续进行安全性评估，同时还需对推理内容进行控制（Chen 等人，2026b）。 智能体对其执行边界的推理能力，并不一定与其遵守用户关于工作时间请求的意愿相匹配；无论是提前返回还是明确进入休眠状态，都不能作为规避监控的证据。 未来的研究应检验这些行为是否能预测其在监督下的表现、智能体是否会在提前完成或等待时告知用户，以及了解自身的生成速度或在更快的推理环境下运行，是否会改善其估算结果。

paragraphs.en: Section 4.1 compares Fable 5.1 in Claude Code with Sol and Astra in Codex, so the model and the harness change together. To separate them, we ran each model in the other’s harness with the campaign’s prompts, clock tool, timer and cutoffs. Fable 5.1 ran in Codex, configured like the campaign’s GPT-5.6 Sol runs at maximum reasoning effort, and GPT-6 Astra ran in Claude Code 2.1.259 with the campaign’s command, changing only the endpoint and model name. Both went through OpenRouter. The tasks were 18 GPQA and HLE questions, six picked because Fable in Claude Code had missed a request under the earlier 0.8–1.25 × \times rule and twelve drawn at random, each asked for 1.25, 5 and 20 minutes, and 16 agentic tasks, four each from Terminal-Bench, TUA-Bench, PPTArena and WildClawBench, at the campaign’s three requests for each. One PPTArena task has only two, because the stage for its shortest request was not available. That makes 101 runs per swapped setup, each compared with the campaign’s run of the same task and request. The agentic runs used the campaign’s own task environments, timing supervisor and checks.
paragraphs.zh: 第4.1节将Claude Code中的Fable 5.1与Codex中的Sol和Astra进行了比较，因此模型和运行环境是同步变化的。 为了将它们区分开来，我们在另一个模型的运行环境中，使用该任务的提示词、时钟工具、计时器和截止时间来运行每个模型。 Fable 5.1在Codex中运行，其配置与任务中GPT-5.6 Sol以最大推理强度运行的方式相同；而GPT-6 Astra则在Claude Code 2.1.259中运行，使用任务的命令，仅更改了端点和模型名称。 两者都通过OpenRouter运行。 这些任务包括18道GPQA和HLE问题：其中6道题是因为Fable在Claude Code中根据之前的0.8–1.25 × \times规则漏答了一道请求，另外12道题是随机抽取的，每道题分别要求1.25分钟、5分钟和20分钟；此外还有16个智能体任务，分别来自Terminal-Bench、TUA-Bench、PPTArena和WildClawBench各4个，均按照任务中针对每个任务的三个请求执行。 其中一个PPTArena任务只有两道题，因为其最短请求对应的阶段不可用。 这意味着每种交换后的配置需要进行101次运行，每次运行都与任务中相同任务和请求的原始运行结果进行比较。 智能体运行使用了任务自身的任务环境、计时监督器和检查机制。

paragraphs.en: Astra in Claude Code declined one TUA-Bench task, which asks it to match faces between photos, at all three requests; Astra in Codex and Fable in both harnesses did it. These six runs are left out, and so are the campaign’s runs of the same task and request, so each model’s two harnesses are compared on the same 98 runs. Some runs ended on their own but then failed one of the campaign’s checks: 28 of Astra’s 44 agentic runs in Claude Code, 12 of them for using subagents, and 8 of Fable’s 44 in Codex. They keep their time and are marked in Table 8 . paragraphs.en: Because the swapped runs went through a different provider, we repeated 35 of Fable’s Claude Code question runs and 20 of Astra’s Codex question runs through OpenRouter, changing only the endpoint (Table 6 , last block). OpenRouter alone also cut Fable’s deviation from 3.78 × \times to 2.95 × \times , about as much as swapping harnesses did, so we compare harnesses mainly by slope. The provider refused three of Fable’s first attempts over OpenRouter, and we reran each once, as in the campaign.

paragraphs.en: Over both kinds of task, Fable ended 1 of 98 runs on time in Codex and 5 of 98 in Claude Code, against 60 of 98 for Astra in Codex (Table 6 ). Codex raises Fable’s within-task slope from 0.03 to 0.19 on the questions and from 0.13 to 0.29 on the agentic tasks. It raises Astra’s as well, from 0.85 to 0.96 and from 0.69 to 0.87. So of the slope gap on these 34 tasks, the harness accounts for about 0.15 and the model for about 0.7: Fable in Codex stays well below Astra in Claude Code on both kinds of task (Figure 5 ). paragraphs.en: In both harnesses Fable does most of its thinking before it looks at the clock, then counts the request from that reading. sents.en: Claude’s runtimes actually happen to average 85 minutes, right around its own flat guess, whereas Codex’s average is around 18 minutes, so the same prior gives a 4 × \times error.
sents.zh: Claude 的运行时间平均为 85 分钟，正好与其固定的预测值相近，而 Codex 的平均运行时间约为 18 分钟，因此相同的先验预测产生了 4 倍（\times）的误差。

paragraphs.en: To distinguish average bias from sensitivity to task duration, we use a compression exponent : the slope β \beta in log ⁡ T ^ = α + β ​ log ⁡ T + ε \log\widehat{T}=\alpha+\beta\log T+\varepsilon , where prediction T ^ \widehat{T} and observed runtime T T use the same units. A slope of zero means the fitted prediction does not vary with runtime; a slope of one means proportional scaling in the fitted relationship, not perfect accuracy. Predictions that are always twice the observed runtime also have slope one. Perfect agreement additionally requires zero intercept and zero residual error. We therefore report the exponent alongside multiplicative bias and prediction error. Both models have low fitted exponents, indicating compressed variation across task durations.

paragraphs.en: To this degree, both agents can answer “how long do tasks like this usually take?” but are unable to answer “how long will this specific run take me?” The weak correlations show that the models appear to reflect the human tendency to apply priors to estimates, giving roughly an hour and a half.
paragraphs.zh: 从这个角度来看，两个智能体都能回答“这类任务通常需要多长时间？”，但却无法回答“这次具体的运行会花我多长时间？”微弱的关联性表明，这些模型似乎反映了人类在估算时倾向于运用先验知识的倾向，给出的时间大约是一个半小时。

paragraphs.en: Asking for a prediction in the same turn as the execution has potential for changing how long the agent works on the problem. paragraphs.en: To ensure the ablation was robust to minor phrasing shifts, we included a fourth arm that swaps semantically equivalent verbs: complete and finish . paragraphs.en: In self-evaluation, Sol consistently overestimates its own performance. On several runs, Sol seems entirely unaware of where it failed, giving itself scores in the mid-90s for runs that actually scored below 50%. In an interesting reversal, Opus 5 underestimates its performance most of the time, typically by more than 10 percentage points. On two runs scoring 99.5% and 96.7%, it gave itself 86% (supplementary Figure 16 ).
paragraphs.zh: 在自我评估中，Sol 始终高估了自己的表现。 在几次运行中，Sol 似乎完全不知道自己失败在哪里，对于实际得分低于 50% 的运行，它给自己打出了 90 分中位数的分数。 有趣的是，Opus 5 大多数时候都低估了自己的表现，通常低估幅度超过 10 个百分点。 在两次分别获得 99.5% 和 96.7% 分数的运行中，它给自己打出了 86% 的分数（补充图 16）。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we used generative AI tools to implement methods, clean and reformat data, support qualitative data analysis, give feedback on the methodology, refine hypotheses and interpret results.
